_doc: Working configurations for the two per-edit LLM hooks that were removed from always-on settings.json. They are correct and functional — they were disabled because they fire on every Edit|Write, creating significant token/API costs on a typical session. Use them when you explicitly want per-edit LLM review (e.g. a high-stakes security audit session) by copying into settings.local.json.
_embed_instructions: Copy the hooks array entries below into the PostToolUse Edit|Write hooks array in .claude/settings.local.json (not settings.json — settings.local.json is gitignored and won't affect teammates). Remove or re-gitignore when done.

hooks._doc: Option A — native prompt: hook. Adds ~2500 tokens to the main context window on every Edit|Write. No subprocess; uses the current session's model. Fast but expensive at scale.
hooks.prompt:
You are a security linter. The hook input JSON below describes a file Claude just wrote. If tool_input.file_path is not under apps/, packages/, infra/, or .claude/scripts/ — or does not end in .ts, .tsx, .js, .mjs, .py, or .sh — return {"decision":"approve"} immediately with no other commentary. Otherwise inspect tool_input.content (Write) or tool_input.new_string (Edit) and decide if it (a) hardcodes a real secret/API key/token (a placeholder or example string in a config file's fallback or .env.example is fine), (b) calls eval() or new Function(), or (c) introduces a clear command/SQL injection. Return JSON ONLY, in the form {"decision":"block","reason":"..."} on a violation, or {"decision":"approve"} otherwise.

Hook input:
$ARGUMENTS

hooks._doc: Option B — subprocess hook via claude -p. Spawns a separate claude process per edit (separate API call + latency). Gives full model/output-format control. The claude_review() function in hooks.py implements this; see DISABLED note in its docstring.
